title: Fernhill's CRM team stopped filing data tickets for every campaign
challenge: Every new audience needed a ticket to the data team and about two weeks of waiting. The profile store in Segment had drifted from the loyalty data in Snowflake.
solution: Moved audience building onto the Snowflake models the data team already owned. The data team modeled loyalty and basket data once, and CRM builds on it without SQL.

results.label: Time to launch a new audience
Audience tickets to the data team

quote.text: Our data team built the models once. Now my team ships audiences the same afternoon we think of them.

title: Vasa kept Segment for tracking and activated its EU warehouse with Hightouch
challenge: Vasa needed paid-media audiences built on order and returns data, but legal didn't want customer data copied out of their EU Snowflake region.
solution: Kept Segment for event collection. Hightouch reads from the EU warehouse and syncs only the fields each destination needs, so no second profile store holds customer data.

results.label: Customer data copies outside the EU warehouse
From signature to first live sync

quote.text: We didn't rip anything out. We stopped copying data around, and that's what got legal to sign off.

title: Northpass chose AI Decisioning on Databricks over a suite it already paid for
challenge: The Salesforce bundle was cheaper on paper, but it meant moving regulated account data into another platform.
solution: Ran AI Decisioning directly on governed Databricks tables. Risk and compliance reviewed one data flow instead of two.

results.label: Data platform for compliance to review

quote.text: Compliance approved it because the data never left the platform they'd already reviewed.

title: Tidewater launched personalized trip offers in a quarter, not a year
challenge: The suite rollout they'd scoped had a 12-month implementation plan before the first campaign.
solution: Used existing booking and loyalty models in Snowflake. AI Decisioning picks the offer and send time for each traveler.

quote.text: We were live before the other vendor would have finished discovery.

title: Halden Care passed its security review with the warehouse as the system of record
challenge: Patient-adjacent data couldn't sit in a second vendor-hosted profile store.
solution: Kept all modeling and identity in Snowflake, with column-level controls on what each sync can send.

quote.text: The security team had one question: where does the data live? The answer was 'where it already lives.'

title: Copperleaf grew subscriber revenue with first-party audiences on BigQuery
challenge: Third-party cookie loss cut ad revenue, and the suite option needed a separate data copy and a long integration.
solution: Built reader-interest audiences from BigQuery and synced them to ad platforms and the paywall tool.

results.label: Audiences built by the marketing team

quote.text: Our editors' data was already in BigQuery. We just needed to use it.

title: Pinegrove unified policyholder identity without a new database
challenge: Policyholders showed up as separate people across auto, home, and life systems.
solution: Ran identity resolution in Snowflake and used the unified profile for cross-sell decisioning.

quote.text: One customer, one record, in the warehouse we already trusted.

title: Sundial cut first-month churn with usage-based lifecycle journeys
challenge: Class bookings and app usage lived in BigQuery, but the messaging tool only saw sign-up data.
solution: Synced weekly usage scores to the messaging tool and in-app personalization.

quote.text: The moment marketing could see who stopped booking classes, retention became their project too.

title: Emberline replaced Segment's profile layer and kept its tracking plan
challenge: Two teams maintained overlapping profiles in Segment and Databricks, and audiences disagreed on counts.
solution: Moved audiences to Databricks models, kept the existing tracking plan, and retired the duplicate profiles in phases.

results.label: Source of truth for audience counts

quote.text: The counts finally match, because there's only one place to count.
